label: Merit order: how the day-ahead price is set
context: Animate the merit-order supply curve of the German day-ahead market and how the uniform clearing price is set, in four phases that loop (about 6 s each), with a phase caption at the top. Axes: x = capacity in GW (0 to 140), y = short-run marginal cost in EUR/MWh (-20 to 260). Phase 1 'Building the stack': blocks slide in one by one from the left, each a rectangle whose width is the available capacity and height the marginal cost, labelled inside or above: solar 0 EUR/MWh 35 GW, wind 0 EUR/MWh 30 GW, run-of-river+biomass must-run 10 EUR/MWh 8 GW, hard coal 90 EUR/MWh 10 GW, CCGT gas 95 EUR/MWh 18 GW, lignite 100 EUR/MWh 12 GW, old gas turbines 150 EUR/MWh 10 GW, oil 230 EUR/MWh 3 GW. Colours: solar #E0A21B, wind #0B4FC0, must-run #138374, coal #3D3D3D, CCGT #D0742B, lignite #7B5534, gas turbines #B4552F, oil #6A47C2. Phase 2 'Demand meets supply': a vertical demand line at 62 GW drops in (ink #04204B, labelled 'demand 62 GW'); the point where it crosses the stack is marked; a horizontal dashed line at that block's cost (hard coal/CCGT boundary ~95 EUR/MWh) runs to the y-axis labelled 'clearing price 95 EUR/MWh'; then every block left of the demand line gets a light fill above its own cost up to the price line, labelled 'inframarginal rent: every accepted seller gets 95'. Phase 3 'Sunny and windy noon': solar block widens to 50 GW and wind to 38 GW (blocks to the right shift right), demand 58 GW now crosses inside the zero-cost renewables, price line falls to 0 and then slightly below to -5 labelled 'price ~0 or negative: renewables set the price'. Phase 4 'Calm winter evening': solar shrinks to 0 and wind to 6 GW, demand 70 GW crosses into the old gas turbines block, price line jumps to 150 labelled 'scarcity: a gas turbine sets the price'. Keep text >= 12 px, white background, no top/right axis lines, axis labels in #3D5F91.

spec.title: Merit order: how the day-ahead price is set
spec.caption: Generators are stacked by rising short-run marginal cost. Demand cuts the stack, and the last accepted block sets one uniform price for every seller. Renewables push the stack right and the price falls. A calm evening pulls it left, and an old gas turbine sets the price. Capacities are illustrative available values chosen so the 95 EUR/MWh crossing at 62 GW is consistent.
